subject.title: auto-reply: /allowlist lets an origin allowlist rewrite another channel

question: Should cross-channel `/allowlist` writes require an explicit global owner identity, or may target-channel allowlist membership confer mutation authority for that target?
rationale: Both choices can close the reported hole, but they establish different long-term trust semantics for ordinary channel allowlists and privileged configuration commands.

options.title: Require explicit global owner
options.body: Reject cross-channel mutations unless the sender matches `commands.ownerAllowFrom` or carries internal `operator.admin` authority.

options.title: Authorize against target scope
options.body: Permit the mutation when the sender independently matches an owner rule derived for the selected target channel and account.

recommendation.title: Require explicit global owner
recommendation.body: Reject cross-channel mutations unless the sender matches `commands.ownerAllowFrom` or carries internal `operator.admin` authority.
